Jacobus Ábraham inhabits a lodger's house which had previously been deserted; pays the Lordship, as a lodger, annually fl. 6, and moreover contributes within the Community like the other lodgers; has a distilling cauldron and from time to time also distills spirits; has no other trade; originating from Gedinga. His consort Susanna has one son; has lived in the place for 4 years.
      Izák Fridrich lives with Jacobus Abraham as a sub-lodger; bears every burden within the Community, like the other sub-lodger; carries on no trade; his consort Catherina, originating from Moravia together with her husband, has one son and 2 daughters; has lived in the place for 7 years; has no servants.
      There follow the Hebrews residing in the suburb of Posony (pp. 470–484.)

      In the Transmontane District,

    Moyzes Izak, of Stomfa, lives as a lodger with the Palatinal subject Joannes Antal; pays him annually a census of fl. 2 d. 50. His consort Theresia, likewise of Stomfa; trades in minor things, cloth and others; has one son, named Josephus, and likewise one daughter, Juditha; with him [lives] his in-law Marcus, originating from Stomffa; has one servant, named Adamus, Moravia; has lived there about 6 years.

Has lived in the place for 7 years.

Lordship annually fl. 250, and the Community fl. 12; besides, he carries on second-class trade, in cloth and spices. His consort Czandl has one son, David; one servant named Lebl, originating from Kucsovics; likewise one maid

21. 1727 [OCR 'l7:!7'] September 10 [OCR 'JO'; date reading uncertain, cf. the dating clause of 12 February 1727 below], Eperjes. Sáros County sends up the census of the Jews.

Census of the Jews living in the county of Sáros:
In the estate of Hertnek, Chaim Moskovics, formerly leaseholder of the lord of Hertnek. At present, owing to the excessive accumulation of his arrears, he leases nothing there, but is working to lease the taverns of the domain of Nagy Sáros. He contributes nothing to the public or to domestic necessities. He has with him his brother Israel, whose son, 4 years old, is named Hersko.
The Jewish tavern-keeper, widow of Josephus Herskovics, pays nothing by way of rent. She sells the manorial drink in wine, beer and brandy and pays nothing to the public or to domestic necessities. By virtue of her contract she had a quarter-session assigned to her to cultivate. Nevertheless, compelled by the miserable state of her widowhood, [she had to] give it up [the sentence is incomplete as printed]. She has with her a brother, Josephus, likewise a Jew.
Salamon Izkovits has a son, Izrael, 2 years old. He holds nothing and pays nothing either to the lord or to the public.
In Fritske, the Jew Lesko Jakubovits [OCR 'Lesleo .Iukubuv'; reading uncertain] is the tavern-keeper of that place. He likewise sells the manorial drink in wine, beer and brandy. He pays no rent to the domain and does not contribute to the public or to domestic necessities. He has a field assigned to him with a capacity of two cubuli, and also a small plot for cabbages. He has a son of ten years.

187

PDF viewer page 190

Source scan
In Bartosfalva, Jacobus Chaim sells manorial beer and brandy in place of rent. He pays nothing for public or domestic necessities and cultivates no session or field. He has three sons, Lesko, Martinus and Josephus, for whose instruction he also maintains a teacher, likewise named Lesko.
In Ossiko, the Jew Koplovits sells the manorial drink by way of rent. He does not contribute to the public and cultivates no field. He has 4 sons, all minors: Aaron, Martinus, Jacobus and Matthias.
In Luco [OCR 'L II C o'; uncertain], Major Jacubovits [so in OCR] sells manorial beer and brandy in lieu of rent. He pays nothing for public or domestic necessities. He has an eighth-session assigned to him.
In Richvald, Abrahamus Vukovics sells manorial wine, beer and brandy and pays nothing to the public. He has an eighth-session given out to him. He has two sons of tender age, Hersko and Mesko.
In Zabava, Jacobus Berek is tavern-keeper and also butcher. He sells the manorial drink in wine, beer and brandy and possesses a quarter-session. He contributes nothing to the public or to domestic necessities. He has a son, Abrahamus, 6 [OCR '(j'] years old, and maintains as servant a relative named Lesko.
In Turnye, Samuel Mihulovits [OCR 'Xlihulovits'] sells the manorial drink in beer and brandy and practises the trade of butcher. He pays nothing for public or domestic necessities. He has a garden assigned to him by contract, and likewise two quarters of rye monthly. He has a son, Lazarus, 5 years old.
In Sverso, Samuel Jakubovits sells the manorial drink, namely wine, beer and brandy. He pays nothing for the public and possesses nothing. He has a son, Jacobus, who is married.
In Hrabszky, Lesko Jezko was formerly leaseholder of Lord Christophorus Korotnoky, paying a rent of Rhenish fl. 100. Now, as the year expires [OCR 'untern cxspirando eidern annus'; garbled], he intends to move elsewhere. He contributes nothing to the public and possesses no field. He has two sons: Isacus, [OCR '()'; age illegible] years old, and the other, Hersko, one year old. He also has with him a relative, Abrahamus.
In Sz?ako [OCR 'Sz nak o'; place name uncertain], Jacobus Simonovits is leaseholder of Lord Christianus Ejszdorffer. He pays by way of rent Hungarian fl. 30 [OCR ':10'; uncertain] annually and contributes nothing to the public. He possesses a quarter-session. He has two sons: one, Jacobus, is married; the other, Israel, is [OCR 'H'; age illegible] years old.
In Vályková [OCR 'V á 1y kóc z'; uncertain], Hersko Moskovits, with his sons called Lesko and Aaron, holds a certain house in a cleared place under a free title of lease. The landlord cleared certain lands for him with a capacity of three cubuli and handed them over to him to cultivate. For this he pays by way of rent Hungarian fl. 21 annually.
In Sandal, Josephus Jalinkovits, with his son Mortha, lives on the deserted holding Pratkovszky but possesses no appurtenances. For the residential house and for selling drink there, for private use, he pays the landlord by way of rent Hungarian fl. 10 annually.
In Porubka, Salamon Leskovits, with his son Marko, lives on the deserted holding Barnyakovszka. Certain lands are provided to him by the landlord field by field, which he cultivates through hired men. In Nyerjes, Lazar Abrahamovits lives on the cottar session Strasovszka. The landlord provides him with lands field by field, which he has cultivated through hired men. He sells his drink from it [syntax unclear in source], and therefore pays the landlord by way of rent Hungarian fl. 30.
In the market town of Zboro lives Hiczko Stiamovits [OCR; uncertain], whose servant, likewise a Jew, is called Jacobus. In Ladomér [OCR 'Lad o m r' with stray 'é'], Mosko Berkovits, with his son called Berko, lives on the deserted holding Hinsakovszka, consisting of 2 virgae. He holds lands and meadows and cultivates them through hired men. Hence, with the toll, the brandy (he does sell the manorial wine) and other benefits, he pays Hungarian fl. 100 annually.
In Krajna Polyana, Jacobus Markovics lives as a sub-tenant with an inhabitant called Ivanisin Ihnat, together with his sons Hitzko, Lejba and Elia Marko [one or two names; uncertain] and also his now decrepit parent. He holds no plot or lands and pays nothing.
In Alsó Komarnyik, Daniel Smulyovics, with his sons Smulyi, Chomka and Chitzko, lives on a certain deserted holding consisting of three virgae. He cultivates the pertaining lands by hire and pays the landlord Hungarian fl. 24 annually.
In Felső Svidnyik, Jacobus Izraelovits, with his son Berko, lives on the deserted holding Hudakovszka. Lands are cut out for him by the domain and are likewise cultivated with manorial assistance. For this he pays the landlord Hungarian fl. 12 annually, and he sells the manorial wine.
In Strocsin, Izrael Herskovits, with his sons Simon and David, lives on the deserted holding Varvorckovszka, consisting of 1½ virgae. He cultivates the lands belonging to that session by hire and sells the manorial wine. For other benefits he pays by way of rent Hungarian fl. 30 annually.
In Hrabovcsik, Elias Jakubovics lives as a sub-tenant with an inhabitant called Vojtsko Fedor. Since he is a newcomer, he leases nothing and holds no means.
In the market town of Kurima, Vulff Salamonovics lives on the curial site. Lands are cut out for him by the domain, which he has cultivated by hire. He sells his drink and holds a brewery, for which [OCR 'iL quo anno'; garbled] he pays the landlord Hungarian fl. 100 annually.

At the castle of Tarcza, on the 12th day of the month of February, 1727.

22. 1728 January 24, Tapsony. Somogy County reports that it has no permanent Jewish inhabitant; however, a Jew, Márton Marx [heading OCR 'jJJ ar» jl[ árton'; text below reads 'Martinum Morx'; uncertain], usually comes from Rohonc to Szigetvár to trade.

"In this County of ours, no Jew is found who has taken up real and fixed residence anywhere, or who is subject to a particular landlord. However, a certain man from the market town of Rohoncz, named Martinus Morx, comes to the fortress of Szigeth for the sake of trade (as is customary). He spends some time there now and then, and then returns to his family settled in Rohoncz. On this account, namely that he has not been incorporated here, he has by no means borne the public burden at present ..."

O. L. Htt. Litt.


23. 1728 March 15, Lőcse. Report of Szepes County on the Jews living in the county:

List of the Jews actually living within this County of Szepes, prepared in conformity with the gracious intimation of the Exalted Royal Lieutenancy Council, through a diligent investigation instituted to that end by the district judges.
In the estate of Huntzdorff two Jews are found. The first, named Samuel Joseph, lives with his wife Juditha. He has no children and no other household except one servant, named Abraham, originating from the Kingdom of Poland.
The other is named Marcus Moyses. He has a wife, Maria, with children named Enoch Moyses and Abraham Moyses. These Jews came from the market town of Bajmócz to the estate of Hozelecz, likewise adjacent to this county. From there they moved to the aforesaid estate of Huntzdorff and have lived there from the feast of St. Michael last past up to the present. Neither of them pays anything to the community of the place, but they pay Hungarian fl. 12 to Lord Paulus Berzeviczy, under whose jurisdiction they are. They carry on trade in fringes, cloth and other wares of that kind of no great importance, and use no fields beyond the plot they inhabit.
In the above-written estate of Hozelecz, in the curia of the widow of the late Egregius Stephanus Okolicsány, resides a third Jew, named Abraham, with his wife Juditha and three male children called Levko, Lazar and Mark. He has no household and [carries on] a rather mean trade with wares of lesser value, namely

190

PDF viewer page 193

Source scan
...practising [a trade], to whom the aforementioned widow [OCR: 'antelatos'] has leased, in the aforementioned manor house, one small room with a chamber, for an annual payment of eight Hungarian florins.

Finally, a fourth Jew was found in the estate of Primocz [OCR: 'Prirnocz'], namely in the manor house of Lord Szent Miklossy, with his wife Barbara and also his sons and daughters Moyses, Joachim, Bertha and Barbara. They practise no trade and keep no household servants, nor do they have any means, seeking their livelihood together with the above-named wife and children only by distilling brandy. For this the aforementioned Lord Szent Miklossy pays one Hungarian florin weekly as wages for the labour, according to the agreement made to that effect. These two Jews mentioned immediately above, having no fields, also do not engage in agriculture, and for that reason contribute nothing toward the support of the local community.

24. 4 February 1728. Simontornya [OCR: 'Simontorns]«']. Report of Tolna County on the Jews residing in the county.

... [instructions] received with submission concerning the Jews, graciously dispatched to us. In order to establish how many there are, who they are and what kind, we sent out to that end our judge of the nobles (Judlium) Lord Joannes Dalmata and the other, Joannes Ferenczfi, our fiscal. They faithfully reported, and in particular the said Lord Dalmata, as follows. In the seigneurial market town called Piuezehely [OCR; possibly Pincehely] belonging to the most serene princely house of Esterházy, a Jew named Ábraham Samuél had a house or dwelling, but kept his wife and children at Rohoncz. He himself trades together with his brothers, namely Jacob and Michael. He holds a house and a vaulted shop (fornix) on lease for twenty florins, though without appurtenances. All three are married, but their womenfolk (as mentioned) live at Rohoncz. They keep one journeyman, likewise one apprentice, and a Sachter. They have already been trading here in our midst for ten years, but have contributed nothing whatsoever to us for public purposes. They have merchandise worth more or less [OCR: 'plus nimis'] a thousand florins. They trade in cloth, silks, 'kopp en-dueh' [OCR; possibly Kopftuch], 'scpbuch' [OCR unclear] and goods of other kinds, and also deal in muslin, linen cloth, laces, paper, sugar, spices and goods of other sorts, as well as salt and oil.

In the market town of Dombovar, which likewise belongs to the most serene princely house, there is Ábraham Isak, a distiller of brandy. He himself pays the lordship sixty denarii per urna, and annually distils more or less [OCR: 'plus nimis'] up to seventy urnae. He came from Moravia. He has a wife and male offspring, namely Jacob, Joachim, Wolffgang, Rubin and the younger Jacob. He keeps a Christian coachman and a Sachter, to whom he pays twenty-four florins annually. He has goods worth about one hundred florins and holds the butcher's shop from the lordship. For seven years he has paid nothing into our [county's] coffers.

In the abbatial market town of Földvar [OCR: 'Földval''] the following are found: Samuél Jacobus; Jacobus, a newcomer, who came there last year, namely 1727; and Elias Marcus, unmarried, who has nothing but one horse. The said Jacobus Samuél came last autumn from Vacino [OCR; reading uncertain] in the illustrious county of Pest, with the lord's licence. His wife is named Anna Rendi, and he has one son, Jacob Samuel. He pays the landlord eighty florins as lease according to the contract. He does nothing else than [OCR: 'quod'] distil brandy, and up to now has paid nothing into our coffers.

O. L. C. 29. No 1. 1728-6.

25. 19 February 1728. Torna. Report of Torna County on the Jewry of the county.

... that formerly no Jews existed within this county of ours, nor did they have fixed residences or dwellings. Now, however, one Jew, named Jacobus Elias, is present in the estate of Nadaska, holding on lease the brewery of the Most Excellent and Illustrious Lord Count General Franciscus Gyulai de Marosnemeti (tit.). On examination he confessed that he was born in Moravia and came from there to the illustrious county of Liptó. He lived there for thirteen years and from there moved directly to this county of ours. He has a wife named Anna Hersly, by whom he has one son named Abraham and two daughters, one Susanna and the other Helena. He also keeps with him a twelve-year-old Jewish orphan boy named Abraham Isac. A tax has been imposed on him for the domestic needs of the county, payable monthly: fl. 1, kr. 30 [OCR: 'Xcifer 30'] ...

O. L. C. 29. No 1. 1728-7.

27a   1727, 13 February. Turócszentmárton. Conscription of the Jews of Turóc County.

In the year 1727, on the 13th day of the month of February. Pursuant to the Determination of the Illustrious Community of this County of Thurocz, issued [lata] in the town of Szent Márton on the seventh day of the month and year written above, on the basis of the gracious Intimation of the Exalted Royal Lieutenancy Council concerning the conscription of the Jews residing within this County, we, the undersigned noble magistrate and juror of the aforesaid County, have conscribed the said Jews in the following manner and order. Namely:

First, in the aforesaid town of Szent Márton there are found:
 1. Isacus Levko with consort, one little son and two daughters living with him.
 2. Mojses, brother of the aforesaid Isacus, with consort, one little son and three daughters.
 3. Jacobus Chyrurgus [surgeon], kinsman by marriage (affinis) of the same Isacus Levko, with his spouse and two sons.
 4. Another Jacobus, son of the oft-repeated Isacus, already having lodging separately with his consort, two little sons and one little daughter.
 5. Josephus, likewise son of the same Isacus placed first, with consort and one little daughter, having his lodging separately.
 6. Abrahamus, son-in-law of the oft-repeated Isacus Levko, with spouse, four little sons and one little daughter.
 7. Marcus Vitrarius [glazier] with consort, two little sons and one little daughter.
 8. Philippus with consort, one little son and two daughters.
 9. Another Abrahamus, Lanio [butcher], with consort, one little son and two daughters.

Second, in Mossóc [OCR garbled: 'IIIo s s Ó c r']:
 Samuel, likewise son of the above-recounted Isacus Levkó, with consort, three little sons and two daughters.

Third, in the town of Szucsán:
 1. Jacobus Beniamin with consort and two daughters.
 2. Daniel with spouse, one little son and two daughters.
 3. Another Daniel, leading a solitary life.

Nicolaus Ilgo, noble magistrate of the aforesaid County of Thurocz, m. p.
Adamus Czeper, juror (iuris assessor) of the same County, m. p.

O. L. Act. part. 43.

      We, the undersigned ordinary judges of nobles and sworn assessors of the Ill. County of Ungh, by virtue of the present acknowledge and attest that, by the gracious mandate of the E. i. L-i C-i R-i [abbreviation unclear], we have listed and recorded the Jews present in our district of Szobrancz in the following manner:
      In Hunkócz, the Jew Gregorius has one son aged three; he lives in the house of the noble lord Georgius Tomcsics and farms the arable lands of his plot, sows; he has two oxen, one horse, a distilling pot, and maintains a Hungarian servant; he pays an annual lease of Hung. fl. 12; to the domestic treasury of the Ill. County he contributes  xr. 21.

      Varallya [OCR: 'Var a II y a'], the Jew Major lives in the house of the noble lord Ladislaus Draveczki, but carries on no husbandry except retailing wine, if he is able to buy it; he pays the aforementioned lord Hung. fl. 6. He has two daughters [Latin 'duos filias', gender inconsistent], one horse, a distilling pot; but because he is now a newcomer, he contributes nothing to the treasury of the Ill. County.
      Vinna, Mosko Jakubovics, is already an old man, having no successors; he has two oxen, one cow, one horse; he does not live on a serf or leased site, but lives by grace among the landlords. Until he was burned out, he paid to the treasury of the Ill. County  xr. 24.
    David Salamonovics has two sons, one called Marko, aged three, the other Barko, aged five; he has one horse, has no other property, and pays no lease to anyone either; but before he was burned out he paid as tax to the treasury  xr. 21.
     On which census and inquiry, made in the foregoing manner, we have issued our present testimonial letters, confirmed with the signatures of our hands and our customary seals.

      Census of the Jewish leaseholders living in the royal fiscal domain of Unghvár, carried out in the following manner:
      In the market town of Unghvár, Jacobus Izraelovics, residing there, has with him a son-in-law and one son aged about 6 [OCR: 'G']; his son-in-law [has] one son aged three; likewise two Jewish servants, Abrahamus Marko and another called Csalin, who have nothing at all, but are merely kept in service. There is moreover another,

212

PDF viewer page 215

Source scan
     Jacobus Marko, who sells beer in the tavern leased by the aforesaid Jacobus Izraelovics, having no property. He has a house in the aforesaid market town of Unghvar, with one vaulted room, where brandy is also usually retailed, with the crossing of the river called Ungh, and moreover in the estate of
      Usok, with a tavern for brandy, mead and beer, where his Jewish lodger also lives; and from here he pays an annual lease of Hung. fl. 200. For this he has three distilling pots, keeps four horses, two cows; he pays tax monthly .... xr. 36; otherwise nothing.
     In the estate of Perecseny, Mendelly Jakubovics, residing there, has two sons, the first aged thirteen, the other eight; one cow, one smaller distilling pot; he has leased a small house with a plot. In the said Perecseny he has arable lands for both rotation fields with a capacity of cubuli [number missing in OCR], hayfields, meadows of three cartloads of hay; hence he pays an annual lease of Hung. fl. 10. Finally he pays tax monthly to the treasury xr. 18.
     In Kis Brezna, Aron Majnovics holds a lease at Hung. fl. 8 annually with a small house, whose plot has no fruit trees; appurtenances of fields in two rotation fields with a capacity of six cubuli, meadows and hayfields of four cartloads. He has one son aged six, one smaller distilling pot, one horse; finally he pays tax monthly to the treasury  xr. 21, and keeps one cow.
      In Nagy Brezna, Ábraham Moskovics holds a lease, together with the lordly mill existing there, at Hung. fl. 30 annually; [he has] two sons, one aged about 14, the other three. He keeps one distilling pot, enjoys the benefit of retailing mead, beer and brandy, inhabits a small house with plot leased in the foregoing manner; there is no yield from the plot, except that for two rotation fields he has lands with a capacity of 8 cubuli, hayfields, meadows with a capacity of three cartloads of hay. Hence he pays tax to the treasury monthly kreuzers  :W. [OCR; amount unclear]
Moreover he keeps two yoke oxen, likewise two cows, and one horse.
   In Sztavna, Froim Josephovics, residing there, has leased a plot with a small house, where no produce is had, at Hung. fl. :30. [OCR; amount unclear], together with the brandy tavern of the estate of Oatuzicza [OCR; place name uncertain]; he has two sons, the first aged about 18, the second about n. [OCR; age unclear]. He keeps one distilling pot, two oxen, one horse, two cows; he enjoys the benefit of retailing mead, brandy and beer. With his aforesaid plot there are fields for both rotation fields with a capacity of six cubuli, hayfields and meadows with a capacity of three cartloads of hay; hence he also pays tax to the treasury of the Ill. County monthly  xr. 21.
      In Lyutta, Pinasz [OCR: 'Piuasz'] Levkovics, having no sons at all, holds a lease at Hung. fl. annually Hi. [OCR; amount unclear]. He has a certain small house with a plot, whose appurtenances do exist, but since he lacks livestock, he cultivates none of them; he keeps, however, one cow and one horse; finally he pays tax from here monthly  xr. 21.
He also enjoys the retailing of brandy, mead and beer.
     In the market town of Unghvár, the Jew Szimcsó, living as a lodger with Stephanus Petroczy, pays no lease, nor tax, since he is a destitute person; he has one son aged about six.

30.               9 May 1728. Zalaegerszeg. Report of Zala County
                            on the Jews residing in the county.

       Specification of the Jews staying in the County of Szala, reported before the Universitas of the same county by the district judges of nobles dispatched to inquire into the matter.
        In the market town of Keszthely, one residing there, named Matthias, has a wife with two sons and one daughter, residing permanently at Rohoncz in the Illustrious County of Vas [Castriferrei]. Likewise he keeps with him one Christian carter, one cart and four horses for transporting his goods of various kinds; besides this he carries on no other husbandry, nor does he cultivate any lands. For the vaulted room or shop for his goods he has hitherto paid annually to lord Volffgangus Bakó, by way of lease, fl. 12. Otherwise he has contributed nothing up to the present for the public subsidy or the domestic necessity of the county.
        In the same place, one named Josephus likewise has a wife, three sons and five daughters, likewise living at Rohoncz; he carries on trade together with the aforementioned Matthias, and therefore also pays the lease jointly.
        Likewise in the same place, Joannes and Isac both have wives, and Joannes also one son, likewise living at Rohoncz. [They have] one Christian servant and three horses, moreover various goods in common, and pay for the vaulted room to Petrus Szücs fl. 8. Another Joannes residing in the same place has a wife, four sons and two daughters, also residing permanently at Rohoncz. Moreover [he has] with him one Christian carter, with a cart and four horses, and goods of various kinds, paying an annual lease to the honourable Franciscus Marton of fl. 12.
        In the market town of Szent Gróth, Jacobus minor Ensl has a wife, no children; a Jewish servant and various goods, and pays the domain a lease of fl. 10.
        In the same place, Jacobus major Hirschl has a wife, two sons, two Jewish servants and one Christian carter; four horses, goods of various kinds; he pays the domain a lease together with the toll of fl. 120.
        Adamus Notl, co-lessee [OCR: 'conquestor'; reading uncertain] and co-toll-farmer, has a wife and three sons; their wives and children also live at Rohoncz.
        There are moreover in the same place the Jews Tobias, David and Hierscl Ensl, because they mostly live there and sell the goods of the aforesaid Jews by distributing them through villages and fairs; they have three horses, but pay nothing to anyone.
        In the market town of Sümegh, Benedictus Marx has with him a son named Abrahamus, another, Leo, [and] one daughter at Rohoncz together with his wife. He has two horses and a cart, with them one Hebrew boy named Adamus; he sells various goods and pays the domain a lease of fl. 12.
        In the market town of Tapolcza, Moyses Marx has a wife, moreover one son and two daughters living at Rohoncz.

  1. 1727, February 19. Szatmárnémeti. Even the only Jew has left the town.

      . . . There are no other Jews living in the bosom of our city except one, named Salamon Moskovics, with his family, who had already held the lease of the brewery for 400 florins for two years; but now, having gone off into the Kingdom of Poland, it is doubtful whether he will ever return.

1727, May [OCR: 'rnu],'; probably máj. = May] 2. Szentgyörgy. The town of Szentgyörgy reports that no Jew lives under the town's jurisdiction, but several live within its territory, in the houses of nobles.

       'Although indeed very many Jews reside within this City, they are nevertheless by no means subject to our Jurisdiction, but dwell here and there in free Curiae, to the manifest burden of the City; these Jews, together with the Inhabitants or Christian Residents there, pay and contribute nothing to the County, much less to the City, except a single one living in a house of the City, who is accustomed to pay annually, in the manner of an Arenda, 200 florins for the support of the City. For these adduced reasons, since the aforesaid Jews were placed outside our Jurisdiction, they could by no means be enumerated by the City.'

     O. L. nu, Litterae. [archive reference as in OCR]

Census of the Jews submitted by the town of Szatmár, dated 16 February 1737.

List of the Jews to be found within the royal and free town of Szathmar Nemethi.

1. The Jew Jacobus Jakabovich, a native of the Kingdom of Poland and of the town of Presch [OCR 'Preseho'; reading uncertain].
He has a wife.
He has six children, namely 3 male and likewise 3 female; one of them, however, is married to the Jew noted below.
He has 3 Christian servants.
Horses: No. 3.
Cows: No. 2.
He states that his landlord in Poland is Prince (tit.) D. D. Lubomirsky.
He states that he pays nothing annually to his said hereditary lord.
To the town, for the public account, for the lease, he paid this year 100 Hungarian florins.
In kind he pays nothing.
He practises no craft.
Nor any trade.
By condition he is the lessee of the town's brewery, to whom the liberty has been granted to sell beer by the barrel and half-barrel, and likewise to distil and sell brandy.

2. The Jew Aaron Izraelovicz, son-in-law of the aforementioned Jew, a native of the town [OCR 'citte'] of Liska in the Kingdom of Poland.
He has no children.
No servant.
No draught animal.
He practises no trade or craft.
He states that his landlord in Poland is the castellan Count Sandemirsky.
He pays his landlord nothing annually.
To the town he pays nothing at all. The condition he professes for sustaining his life is that of seller of the beer and brandy of the aforesaid lessee.

       [OCR: 'Oiroa'; probably 'Circa'] Concerning the item of what they pay annually to the hereditary lord, the Jews declared that what had been specified above is paid to the community of the Jews of Huno-brod [Latin: Huno-brodensium], and that out of this payment the census of the landlord, the public burdens which they owe to the Margraviate of Moravia, and also their Rabbis are paid. To this end he permits them to exact a certain tax from foreign Jews [OCR: 'eotum'; word unclear] at the town gates at the military watches, as if in aid of the aforesaid payment, to the prejudice of the town, for the remedy of which a humble petition is made.

3a. 30 June 1744. Baja. In Bács county Jews live only in Baja and Pétervárad.

      What the status and condition of the Jews dwelling within this county at Baja and Petrovaradin was ... we had most humbly represented. Accordingly, while continuing to adhere to the legal usage and practice concerning the tax customarily paid by these same Jews both for the domestic and internal needs of the county and for the expenses of the militia to be raised by the county, nevertheless, the indispensable necessity of the present war circumstances having been further declared by means of another gracious intimation of the same E. R. L. C. [Excelsum Regium Locumtenentiale Consilium] ..., and ourselves seeing it most clearly, we determined that the said Jews are also to be taxed extraordinarily, in the same amount as they pay for the ordinary needs of the county, for a quota to be paid to the royal treasury on account of the present war circumstances. The Jews of Baja customarily pay a tax of 10 f., those of Petrovaradin 75 f., together 85 f.; they are to contribute the same amount to the royal treasury as well. Their specific and individual census would be clearly evident from these annexes.

                       Petition of the Jews of Győr County to the county.

     With the deepest submission we are compelled to represent that ... we all would gladly satisfy the Gracious Will of the aforesaid Sacred Royal Majesty in accordance with our strictest obligation; but since there are among us such persons, namely Josephus HiersI, Simon Samuel, Simon Gerschl, Moyses Hierschl [OCR: 'Ioyses'], and Philippus David, all in Föllpéc, likewise Lebel Isaak in Eöttevény, and finally a Hebrew woman, the wife of a barber, abandoned by her husband with her children, in Koronczo — all of them Jews dwelling in estates situated in the aforesaid County of Győr — who are entangled in such straits of misery and, respectively, afflicted by continual illnesses, that unless they were relieved by the help of others in providing their daily bread, they would certainly have to perish of hunger; consequently, by reason of impossibility, they would be able to pay nothing at all.
     N. N., Jews dwelling here and there in this County of Győr.
      Given at our general assembly held in Győr (Jaurini) on the 8th day of the month of April in the year one thousand seven hundred and forty-five, the Community of the County of Győr.

12. 1745, September HJ [OCR unclear]. Turócszentmárton. In Turóc County the only Jewish resident is a surgeon; he too is being expelled.
      Since the time when, according to the gracious intimation of the E. C. R. L. [Royal Lieutenancy Council], the Jews were removed from this County of Turóc several years ago, none have their fixed residence here who could be taxed, except one, a needy surgeon, residing in Thurán for some short time; but so that we may satisfy in this respect too the gracious intimation of the same E. C. concerning the removal of the said Jews, we have ordered him too, through one of our noble magistrates, to depart and not presume to take up a permanent residence in this county ...
     Given from our general assembly held at the usual place in the market town of Szent Márton, on the Hi [OCR unclear] of September [7-bris], 1745.
                                               The Universitas of the County of Turóc.

of Bazin [Boziniensis].

2a. 30 June 1744. Bártfa. In the town of Bártfa there is one single [OCR 'serlóző' — word unclear] Jew.

...last year, the matter of the taxation and individual conscription of these [Jews] was left in abeyance [OCR 'omansisse'; reading uncertain], solely because in that same year no Jew having a domicile or residence was found within this town; consequently the execution of what had been graciously ordered could not follow

[p.] 714

PDF viewer page 716

Source scan
[could not follow.] But so that we may be seen to have satisfied our most humble obligation, ... we signify that there is for now one Jew lingering here, who on 22 May of the current year leased the benefit of retailing spirits. Whether this same Jew should be held, for the coming term of St Michael the Archangel, to payment of the whole six florins computed for one year, or should be compelled to pay for half a year only, namely three florins (since he had fixed such a period for his stay here), we most humbly submit to the higher judgement and determination of the aforesaid Excellent Royal Council [OCR 'E-i O-i R-i']...

Bartpha, 30 June 1744.

2b. 21 January 1745. The town of Bártfa's detailed report on the single Jewish family.

The Jew Josephus Herskovics, married, has 2 sons, one 18 years old, the other 8 years old; 3 minor daughters; two Jewish servants, one unmarried, the other married; 1 Christian maidservant; 1 Jewish maidservant; no teacher; 1 Christian distilling spirits. He pursues no trade and knows no craft; the aforementioned son of 8 years, however, he has in Poland.

He has no horse, no oxen, 2 cows.

His hereditary lord in the Kingdom of Poland is Zamonszky, residing in the town called Zamoscs, to whom at present [he pays] nothing; to the royal treasury, however, he pays a tax of () Rhenish florins [figure missing in OCR], and to the illustrious County of Sáros 24 Rhenish florins; to the Kingdom of Poland, however, he pays annually 2 gold pieces.

To the aforenamed town he pays, from the revenue of spirits and of the mills, an arenda or rent of 1791 Rhenish florins 40 kreuzers [OCR; figure may be misread], nothing in kind, but he is obliged to contribute from his livestock.

Bartpha, 21 January 1745.
Judge, consul and senate of the Royal Free Town of Bártfa.

Htt. Acta Jud. f. 992. (225-227)

5. 16 [OCR 'IG'] March 1745. Kőszeg. Only one Jew lives in the town of Kőszeg.

In this town only one single Jew resides, whom we would gladly have had removed, but he is maintained by the Caroline privilege. He pursues trade and owns a house, and contributes from these; his son-in-law, living with him in one household, is a help to him. Hence, apart from the contribution, he has not yet been taxed; regarding his extraordinary taxation we shall conform to the disposition of the exalted authority; regarding his extraordinary taxation we shall most humbly conform to the disposition of the exalted authority [sentence repeated in the source]...

Judge and senate of the Free and Royal Town of Keössegh, or Ginsium.
Ginsium, in the senate, on the 16th [OCR 'Hi-a'] of March.

6a. 19 July 1743. Modor [OCR 'ilf odor']. The town of Modor sends a report on two Jews.

...only two Jews are found, separate from each other in livelihood and trade, of whom one,

Jacobus Schaja Hirschil, since he owns both a house and small means, [is to bear the common burdens] from these as well as from his trade, which he conducts chiefly in cloth and other smaller materials; the other, however, his relative by marriage,

[p.] 718

PDF viewer page 720

Source scan
Marcus Moyses, living with him as a lodger, from his trade alone, which he likewise pursues in small things, — [both] ought to bear the common burdens proportionately.

For although they trade in small things incapable of bringing great profit, nevertheless, whenever the reason and necessity of some imposition or apportionment demands it, they are compelled to contribute proportionately to the common fund of the citizens: the former both from his house and other means and from his trade, the latter from his trade alone, since he possesses nothing else...

Modra, 19 July, in the year 1743.
Judge, consul and senators ... of the town of Modor.

Htt. Acta Jud. f. 992. (72-73)


6b. 5 April 1745. Two Jews live in the town of Modor, but only one of them was able to pay the 6 Ft.

List of the Jews residing in the Free Royal Town of Modor:

Jacobus Schaja Hirschil, with his wife, has a house in the town with small appurtenances, from which he renders portions and other dues to the town. He pursues trade in cloth, in laces which they call Mazolán, and in such smaller things; from time to time, according to his custom and ability, in raw hides and wool.

Moyses Marcus, with his wife and four children, living in the house of the former; a lodger, he has no means and pursues no trade of his own, but assists the above-specified, as his relative by marriage, like a servant.

Judge, consul and senate of the Free Royal Town of Modor.
Modra, 5 April, in the year 1745.

In the [OCR: 'Hséró'; probably 'kísérő' = accompanying] document Pest county requests the abolition of the new tax:

That Your E. C. R. L. [abbreviation as in source] may deign to interpose its offices with Her Sacred Imperial-Royal Majesty to this effect: however much the aforesaid Jews, at present tolerated in this kingdom, may have been of some domestic utility to the landlords, nevertheless, before the capitation tax is in any way introduced into this kingdom through them, may she rather deign, by that Maternal Imperial-Royal benevolence in which the estates of the realm, in confidence of their homagial subjection, have fully grounded their subjects' hope, to forbid them all entirely from the kingdom. For since they dwelt on the lands of the landlords reserved for the landlords' own account and not subject to conscription, and since agreement had been reached generally throughout the kingdom concerning the contributional quantum, and the law itself, assigning them to the internal benefit of the counties, exempted them to that extent, it would not be without the greatest prejudice both to the private rights of the landlords and to the public [interest] that they should be compelled to pay a contribution to the royal treasury under any title whatsoever, and in particular this capitation, and be drawn away from the domestic fund [cassa domestica] through impoverishment, and that the landlords be deprived of their rents. These things [we submit] not from any slackening of our faithful zeal, always promptly expended, as occasions allow, in the promotion of the service of Your Imperial-Royal [Majesty] ... [text breaks off / OCR]

Given at Pest, from our general assembly held on the tenth day of the month of October in the year one thousand seven hundred and forty-six.
The community of the counties of Pesth, Pilis and Solth, united by law [articulariter].

HU. Acta Jud. f. 992. (340-347)

            We did indeed order, also on the occasion of our last general assembly, that the appointed collector should endeavour to collect the resulting quota from those as well who are still in arrears and are recorded in the aforementioned list marked with letter A.), under threat of a military execution to be issued immediately; but our efforts fell to nothing [OCR 'in initum eeeldere', presumably 'in irritum cecidere'], for their exhausted state, reduced to beggary,

 794

PDF viewer page 796

Source scan
did not permit them to be able to satisfy their aforesaid obligation.
     Matters therefore standing thus, as we have justly to fear lest the burden of the military execution soon to be issued should fall not upon these, as having altogether nothing and thus unable to pay even the execution quota, but upon others who have amply satisfied their obligation, with grave loss also to the contribution fund ... may [it] deign to interpose its gracious offices with Her Sacred Majesty [OCR 'S.-m M-m Som'], so that she may graciously deign to remit the resulting quota of our wretched Jews, who are thus unable to pay ...
    At our general assembly held continuatively in the Free Royal City [L. R. C.] of Posonium, in the year one thousand seven hundred and forty-seven, on the eighth day of August.

      ... we have indeed had the census of the Jews carried out, as we enclose it; but as soon as they noticed the completion of this census, being in any case provided with scant means, and with no guard on the passes holding them back, they slipped away, with grave damage also to the landowners through thefts committed, so that barely half of them remained, with the capitation sum carried off [Latin 'cum summa capitationali asportata'; sense ambiguous]. As much as we were able to have collected, we diligently applied ourselves to that; we therefore most humbly have to beg the E. C. R. L. [presumably the Exalted Royal Lieutenancy Council] to deign to interpose its gracious offices with Her Sacred Majesty, lest the tax of such fugitive Jews should in some measure redound upon the wretched common people, already burdened with great burdens ...

1746. VII. 13. Bussócz. We, the undersigned, acknowledge by virtue of the present letter that when on the 8th day of the month of July of the year written below ... we went out to the sites of the possessions of this County of Szepes noted below for the conscription of the Jews, then and there, on the aforesaid day, we made the conscription as follows, their number following in this manner. Namely:
In the possession of Humizdorj] [OCR reading; place name uncertain],
Mojses Billicer with his wife Maria has minor children: 1 male, 2 female.
Valo Markus, with his wife, has 1 son, 2 daughters.
Abraham Marcus with his wife has 2 minor sons. Israel Jacob with his wife, without children.
Mojses Marcus with his wife has 1 minor son. Another Mojses Marcus junior, with his wife Sara, has 1 daughter.
Josephus Level with his wife, son-in-law of the aforesaid Mojses, is without children.
Josephus Samuél with his wife has 2 sons, 2 daughters. His son-in-law Pinkus Mojses with his wife Ester is without children.
The teacher (praeceptor) Simon Mojses, with his wife Juditha, has 2 sons, 1 daughter.
Isac Slachter (!) with his wife is without children.
Marcus Ábraham with his consort has 1 minor son.

22b. 1 August 1746. Nagymihály. The főispán of Ung County sends in the census of the Jews, indicating that apart from a shortfall of 32 [OCR '8"!'] Ft he has had the tax of 2 Ft per head collected, and has had it paid in at Kassa.

... The collected sum rises to 400 florins, which I transmit today to Cassovia to the military war treasury. There remain still :t:! [OCR; probably 32] florins, which, because the destitute part of the Jews was unable to pay even after execution was applied, I shall, if Your Sacred Royal Majesty insists, have proclaimed in that county by Your gracious edict.
Since, however, sheer incapacity and poverty have stood in the way, it might perhaps be overlooked, since the county of Ungh, owing to the barrenness of the soil in which it is situated by nature, does not have Jews engaged in trade; rather, those who have migrated 5D [OCR; probably 'from'] neighbouring Poland into the bosom of this county are known to work only as leaseholders of spirits (cremati arendatores) beneath the mountains, chiefly in Ruthenian villages ...
